irac.issue: Whether the West Bengal Tax on Entry of Goods into Local Areas Act, 1970, is valid and whether the tax levied on tea is payable by the tea garden or the tea factory.
irac.rule: The legislative competence of the State Legislature to enact the West Bengal Tax on Entry of Goods into Local Areas Act, 1970, and the validity of the tax levied on tea under the Act.
irac.application: The Supreme Court applied the principles of taxation and legislative competence to determine that the State Legislature has the competence to enact the Act and that the tax levied on tea is payable by the tea factory and not the tea garden.
irac.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the West Bengal Tax on Entry of Goods into Local Areas Act, 1970, is valid and that the tax levied on tea is payable by the tea factory and not the tea garden.
